messages:
alex: Heads-up — after yesterday's kernel selector tweak I see a ~10% p50 regression for seq=256 in prod and p95 micro-spikes for small requests. Attaching traces.

maria: saw that too. I grabbed an nsys capture around 03:12 UTC. Timeline shows a flood of tiny matmul kernels (<50us) interleaved with host-side 'kv_sweep' activity.

sam: that pattern usually means kernel-selection thrash + KV cache sweep work happening on the hot path. The runtime keeps oscillating between the small-cutlass path and fallback kernels.

irene: can you paste the perfetto link / nsys snippet?

alex: perfetto: https://perfetto.app/trace/abcd and GCS: gs://redwood-traces/2169009999/nsys-rep.nsys-rep. here's the nsys summary I pulled: 

```
nsys stats --report gputrace --input trace.nsys-rep
Top kernels:
  gemm_small_kernel     calls: 2200  avg: 48us
  cutlass_matmul_s      calls: 1100  avg: 52us
Scheduling overhead total: 120ms

Host events: kv_sweep: periodic full-trie sweep every 100ms, blocks epoll ~0.9-1.2ms
```

maria: interesting — the kv_sweep periodicity lines up with the latency spikes. our sampler does a full sweep when miss_rate > 3% (old heuristic).

sam: I re-ran locally with `--workload=short-reqs --seq=32` and nvprof shows queue_time dominating compute_time: 

```
nvprof --metrics achieved_occupancy kernel_trace.out
Kernel gemm_small_kernel: avg time 47us, occupancy 34%
Queue time avg: 320us
Total host scheduling jitter: ~1.1ms spikes
```

irene: Queue time >> kernel time — that's the costly bit. Could be continuous batching window too small so we spin many small kernels, and KV sweep steals CPU causing epoll delays.

zach: candidate mitigations: increase min_batch_window_ms for small-paths from 2ms -> 8ms; make kv_sweep incremental (N=32 per pass) vs full-trie; and add a kernel-selection dampener to avoid flipping choices too often.

alex: quick experiment: bumping min_batch_window locally fixed p50 but not p95. Perfetto shows host-side kv_sweep blocking epoll for ~1.1ms exactly when p95 spikes occur.

perf-bot: Incident created INC-2169. Linked traces attached to incident.

maria: also note kernel-selection heuristic: if occupancy < 40% and seq_len < 64 we pick cutlass_small which has low compute but higher launch overhead when called repeatedly. That amplifies the queue/compute imbalance.

sam: proposed action list: 
  - throttle kv_sweep: incremental sweeps + yield to epoll after each chunk
  - add adaptive min_batch_window: EWMA(queue_time/compute_time) => scale window up when queue_time fraction is high
  - cap kernel-choice flips (e.g., once per 1000 calls or cooldown 500ms)
  - prototype coalescer: combine up to 128 micro-requests into a single matmul when aggregate size allows

irene: prioritize: 1) throttle kv_sweep (low risk), 2) cap kernel flips (small change), 3) adaptive batch window (requires more tuning).

alex: I'll open a PR for kv_sweep throttling (kv_sweep_rate config, default 32) and add a tiny yield-to-epoll after each chunk. PR will include a perf test harness.

sam: I'll push the coalescer prototype branch — it buffers micro-requests up to 1.5ms/128 items and issues a fused matmul. Locally it reduces kernel calls 6x for short workload.

zach: testing plan: run sustained 10k qps with seq=32 short payloads, collect nsys + perfetto, compare queue_time/compute_time ratios and kernel call counts. Use trace name `kv-sampler-experiment-2169009999`.

maria: add a unit test to ensure sweeps don't block epoll: simulate heavy-miss pattern and assert max_block_time < 0.5ms.

alex: thanks — I'll post PR link and perf numbers once I have them. If anyone wants to triage traces tonight ping @sam or @maria. :thumbsup:

zach: fyi I also checked our kernel cache warming: we sometimes evict small kernels from JIT cache under memory pressure, causing cold-launch spikes. I'll include a small prewarm of the small-kernel variant during startup for the short-request path.

maria: great — that + kv_sweep throttling should cover host-blocking and launch churn.

alex: timeline: kv_sweep PR today, kernel flip cap tomorrow, adaptive window after we've got baseline metrics. we’ll run canary on dedicated pool.

sam: noted. I'll schedule the 10k qps run and attach traces.

irene: awesome. keep updates here and drop the PR links.
